what_its_for: Pazopanib is a cancer-fighting medicine used to treat advanced kidney cancer (renal cell carcinoma) and certain soft tissue tumors (soft tissue sarcoma). It works by blocking signals that help cancer cells grow and by cutting off the blood supply that feeds the tumor.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablets whole with a full glass of water. Do NOT crush, break, or chew the tablets. Take pazopanib on an EMPTY STOMACH — at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after eating a meal. Try to take it at the same time every day. Do not take it with food, as food significantly increases the amount of medicine absorbed into your body and can cause more side effects.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 800 mg (two 400 mg tablets) taken by mouth once daily. Your doctor may lower your dose to 400 mg or 200 mg if you have side effects or certain health conditions. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and there are MORE than 12 hours until your next scheduled dose, take it as soon as you remember. If there are 12 hours or LESS until your next dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose at the regular time. NEVER take two doses at once or double up to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store pazopanib tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep them away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep all medicines safely out of the reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating grapefruit or drinking grapefruit juice while taking this medicine, as it can raise the level of pazopanib in your blood to a dangerous level. Avoid taking antacids or acid-reducing medicines (like omeprazole, esomeprazole, or Tums) close to your pazopanib dose without asking your doctor first — they can reduce how well this medicine works. Avoid taking blood thinners, certain antibiotics, antifungals, or seizure medicines without checking with your doctor or pharmacist, as many drugs can interact with pazopanib. Avoid becoming pregnant while on this medicine, as it can seriously harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 2 weeks after your last dose. Men should use contraception as well.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience any of the following: yellowing of the skin or eyes (signs of liver problems), severe stomach or abdominal pain, unusual bleeding or bruising, coughing up blood, vomiting blood or blood in your stool, chest pain or pressure, sudden severe headache, sudden changes in vision, weakness or numbness on one side of the body (signs of stroke), signs of a heart attack, severe high blood pressure, painful or swollen hands and feet (hand-foot syndrome), signs of a wound that will not heal, or any signs of serious infection such as fever above 100.4°F (38°C), chills, or feeling very unwell. Also let your doctor know about any persistent diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, fatigue, or hair color changes.
when_it_works: Pazopanib does not cure cancer, but it is designed to slow or stop the growth and spread of cancer cells. You may not feel any different when it is working because it works inside your body at the cellular level. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular blood tests and imaging scans (like CT scans). Some patients begin to see benefits within the first few months of treatment. It is very important to keep taking this medicine every day, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): Pazopanib can be used in older adults, but they may be more sensitive to side effects such as fatigue, high blood pressure, and decreased appetite. Liver problems: If you have moderate or severe liver disease, this medicine may not be safe for you or your dose will need to be significantly reduced. Kidney problems: Mild to moderate kidney disease usually does not require a dose adjustment, but your doctor will monitor you closely. Pregnancy: Do NOT take pazopanib if you are pregnant. It can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby. Tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant during treatment. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for at least 2 weeks after your last dose, as it may pass into breast milk and harm your baby. Children: The safety and effectiveness of pazopanib in children have not been established, and it is generally not recommended for patients under 18 years of age.
